questions.question: How do you annotate collections and generic types in Python?
questions.title: Collection and Generic Type Hints
questions.direct_answer: Annotate collections with their element types using built-in generics (3.9+): list[int], dict[str, User], set[str], tuple[int, ...]. For optional values use X | None (3.10+) or typing.Optional[X]. For a function generic over a type, use typing.TypeVar with TypeVar('T') and declare def first(items: list[T]) -> T. Union types use X | Y (3.10+) or typing.Union[X, Y]. These let you express 'a list of ints' or 'a dict mapping strings to Users' precisely, which mypy uses to catch type errors.

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether you can annotate collections with element types (list[int], dict[str, User]), optionals (X | None), unions (X | Y), and a generic function (TypeVar).
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Using bare list/dict (no element type — loses precision) or the old typing.List[int] (unnecessary on 3.9+).
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: list[int], dict[str, User], set[str], tuple[int, ...] (element types); X | None for optional; TypeVar for generics; X | Y for unions.

sections.title: What the interviewer wants

sections.title: Collections with Element Types
sections.content: Annotate collections with their element types using built-in generics (Python 3.9+): list[int] is a list of ints, dict[str, User] maps strings to User, set[str] is a set of strings, and tuple[int, ...] is a tuple of any number of ints. For optional values use X | None (3.10+) or typing.Optional[X]. For unions use X | Y (3.10+) or typing.Union[X, Y]. For a function generic over a type, use typing.TypeVar: declare T = TypeVar('T') and def first(items: list[T]) -> T to express 'a list of T returning T.' These let you say precisely 'a list of ints' or 'a dict mapping strings to Users,' which mypy uses to catch type errors. Bare list or dict (no element type) loses precision and is discouraged.

sections.title: Anatomy of a Collection Annotation
sections.content:
list[int] = list of ints; dict[str, User] = string→User map; tuple[int, ...] = any-length tuple.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  L[list int] -->|element type| I[int]
  D[dict str, User] -->|key, value| S[str] & U[User]
  O[X \| None] -->|optional| X & N[None]
  G[TypeVar T] -->|generic| F[list T -> T]
```

sections.title: Collections, optionals, unions, and a generic
sections.content:
```python
from typing import TypeVar

# (1) COLLECTIONS with element types (built-in generics, 3.9+).
nums: list[int] = [1, 2, 3]
users: dict[str, User] = {"ada": User()}      # str -> User
tags: set[str] = {"a", "b"}
many: tuple[int, ...] = (1, 2, 3)             # any-length tuple of ints

# (2) OPTIONAL: X | None (3.10+) or Optional[X].
name: str | None = None                       # may be a str or None

# (3) UNION: X | Y (3.10+) or Union[X, Y].
id: int | str = 7                             # int or str

# (4) GENERIC function with TypeVar.
T = TypeVar("T")
def first(items: list[T]) -> T:               # works for any list
    return items[0]
xs = first([1, 2, 3])                         # inferred T = int
```

sections.title: Common Mistakes
items: Using bare list/dict (no element type) — loses precision; mypy can't check element types.
Using the old typing.List[int]/typing.Dict[...] — unnecessary on 3.9+; use built-in list/dict.
Forgetting tuple[int, ...] for a variable-length tuple vs tuple[int, int] (a fixed pair).

sections.title: Key Takeaways
items: Annotate collections with element types: list[int], dict[str, User], set[str], tuple[int, ...].
Optional: X | None (3.10+) or Optional[X]; Union: X | Y (3.10+) or Union[X, Y].
Generic function: TypeVar('T') and def f(items: list[T]) -> T.
Avoid bare list/dict (no element type) — it loses precision for mypy.
Use built-in list[int]/dict[...] (3.9+), not the old typing.List/typing.Dict.

sections.title: Spoken Answer
sections.content: Annotate collections with their element types using built-in generics from Python 3.9: list of int is a list of ints, dict of str and User maps strings to User, set of str is a set of strings, and tuple of int and ellipsis is a tuple of any number of ints. For optional values use X pipe None from 3.10 or typing.Optional of X. For unions use X pipe Y from 3.10 or typing.Union of X and Y. For a function generic over a type, use typing.TypeVar: declare T equals TypeVar of T and def first of items colon list of T returns T to express a list of T returning T. These let you say precisely a list of ints or a dict mapping strings to Users, which mypy uses to catch type errors. The common mistakes are using bare list or dict with no element type, which loses precision and lets mypy not check element types, using the old typing.List of int which is unnecessary on 3.9 plus, and confusing tuple of int and ellipsis, a variable-length tuple, with tuple of int comma int, a fixed pair.
